summary.one_liner: xh is a fast, friendly command-line HTTP client written in Rust that reimplements much of HTTPie's syntax and design.
summary.what_it_does: xh sends HTTP requests from the terminal using HTTPie's request-item syntax for JSON or form body fields, headers, query strings, and file uploads. It supports GET, POST, PUT and other methods, reading request bodies from stdin or files, and downloading responses to a file with -d and -o. Output can be filtered to headers, body, or metadata, and colored with selectable styles. It also offers sessions, basic/bearer/digest auth, proxies, custom TLS certificates, HTTP/2 and HTTP/3 options, Unix sockets, and a --curl flag that prints the equivalent curl command. The README says it aims to be faster than HTTPie, with improved startup speed and a single statically linked binary.
use_cases: send HTTP requests from the command line
test REST APIs with JSON bodies
convert an HTTP request into a curl command
replace HTTPie with a faster client
stack: Rust (Rust 1.85 or later for cargo install)
notable: Drop-in-style reimplementation of HTTPie's request-item syntax (=, :=, ==, @, :)
Built-in --curl flag translates requests into curl commands
Runs as HTTPie-compatible when invoked as http/https, or with XH_HTTPIE_COMPAT_MODE
Binary named xhs or https defaults to HTTPS requests
Single statically linked binary with HTTP/2 support
caveats: Not all HTTPie features are implemented, per the README's disadvantages list
Some package-manager builds use native-tls only
The README describes the project as relatively immature compared with HTTPie
